title: East Finchley & Fortis Green
intro: Two ancient woods within a short walk, one of Britain's oldest cinemas on the High Road, and Hampstead Garden Suburb and Kenwood just over the hill.

items.name: Highgate Wood
items.blurb: Ancient oak and hornbeam woodland looked after by the City of London since 1886, with shady paths, a playground, a cricket field and a café.
items.tip: The café by the playing field has outdoor tables under the trees.

items.name: Kenwood House
items.blurb: An 18th-century villa remodelled by Robert Adam on the edge of Hampstead Heath, with an art collection including Rembrandt and Vermeer and lawns sweeping down to a lake.
items.tip: Entry to the house is free; book ahead at busy times.

items.name: Coldfall Wood
items.blurb: Ancient hornbeam woodland on the Fortis Green side, a Local Nature Reserve with a stream running through it.
items.tip: The paths get muddy after rain: boots help.

items.name: Phoenix Cinema
items.blurb: Opened in 1910 and one of the oldest cinemas in Britain still showing films, with a 1930s auditorium. It is run as a charity.

items.name: Hampstead Garden Suburb
items.blurb: A garden suburb begun in 1907 and planned by Raymond Unwin, with Arts and Crafts houses, hedged lanes and Edwin Lutyens' churches on Central Square.
items.tip: Central Square and the lanes around it are the best part for a stroll.

items.name: Queen's Wood
items.blurb: A steep, wild ancient wood across the road from Highgate Wood, with a community café and organic garden at its edge.
items.tip: Combine it with Highgate Wood for a longer woodland loop.

items.name: Cherry Tree Wood
items.blurb: A small ancient wood right next to East Finchley station, with a playground, tennis courts and woodland paths.
items.tip: Ideal for a short walk on the way to or from the Tube.

items.name: The Archer, East Finchley station
items.blurb: The station was rebuilt by Charles Holden in the late 1930s and is crowned by Eric Aumonier's statue of an archer aiming towards central London.
items.tip: The Northern line from here runs straight to Moorgate.
